mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 1.5% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to tightened financial conditions and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% in the month before the decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior month's mean (t-test p > 0.05) during a rising-rate regime.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 60-day forward return as higher unemployment signals weaker consumer demand and corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.5 percentage points for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly below the 30-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05) during the two-month high-unemployment window.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real GDP chainless) exceeds INDPRO by at least 10 percentage points for three consecutive months, it indicates a demand-led expansion that is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 - INDPRO >= 10pp for three consecutive months
regime_hint: Economic expansion with strong demand pull
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the three-month demand gap window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 5 percentage points for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 60-day forward return as it reflects contracting supply capacity and potential overvaluation.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 5pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly below the prior 30-day average (t-test p > 0.05) during the supply contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.3% in a single month, followed by a FEDFUNDS hold in the next month, the S&P 5-day forward return is expected to be positive as the market anticipates reduced rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% and FEDFUNDS remains flat in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the identified pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (labor market activity) below 145,000 in a month coinciding with a 3-month UNRATE decline below 4% is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return as it signals weak labor market absorption.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 145,000 AND UNRATE < 4% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the defined labor weakening pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive rise in HOUST (housing starts) above 1,200K while UNRATE remains below 5% predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as it reflects resilient housing demand in a low-unemployment environment.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 1,200K for two consecutive months AND UNRATE < 5% in both months
regime_hint: Resilient housing demand in soft labor market
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the pattern.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where UNRATE > 5% for three consecutive months and INDPRO is flat, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent weak labor absorption and muted supply recovery.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% for three consecutive months AND INDPRO is flat
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly below the prior 30-day average (t-test p > 0.05) during the regime.
